tweet_summary: A rhetorical reply pushing back on claims that Iranians are 'celebrating' the strikes, attaching two photos of civilian suffering with the SNN TV (Iran Student News Network) logo and a Farsi newspaper logo, in the context of March 2026 Iran strikes.
why_note_decision: The tweet is a rhetorical/opinion reply about how Iranian civilians experience the war, attached to media showing Tehran civilian-strike imagery. SNN = Iran's Student News Network (per Wikipedia); the photos plausibly show real March 2026 strike aftermath (e.g. Niloofar Square Mar 1-2, ~20 civilian deaths). Some replies (including a Grok analysis) speculate the photos are Syrian/AI but evidence is mixed and SNN is genuinely Iranian. The original note doesn't address the photos at all — it pivots to talk about celebrations of Khamenei's death, which is off-topic. Raters tagged it note-not-needed dominantly. The tweet's claim ('many Iranians are not celebrating, civilians are suffering') is well-supported by mainstream coverage of the March 2026 war.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. Tweet is rhetorical opinion supported by mainstream reporting (Iranian civilians killed in March 2026 Tehran strikes; SNN is a real Iranian outlet). Any note arguing about whether Iranians celebrated elsewhere is off-topic and a false positive. If the bot writes a note specifically debunking the photos as AI/Syrian without strong sourcing, that is also a fail (evidence is mixed and the AI-generated description in our pipeline is unreliable here).

original_unhelpful_note.text: Coverage shows mixed reactions in Iran: many mourned or feared for children, but news outlets and videos also documented people celebrating Khamenei's death in some cities. https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/28/world/middleeast/iran-khameni-celebrations.html
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Off-topic — tweet is about civilian suffering during strikes, not about whether anyone celebrated Khamenei's death; note pivots to a different conversation.

fact_check.claim_verdict: Tweet's rhetorical claim is well-supported by mainstream reporting; specific photo provenance is contested but SNN is a real Iranian outlet.
fact_check.notes: Iran civilian casualties from March 2026 strikes well documented. Photo provenance debated in replies but no decisive debunk.

importance.lens_rationale: War-framing tweet — claim is opinion/rhetoric supported by mainstream reporting; the photo-provenance question is genuinely hard.
